reason: 423 of 442 responses are fixed boilerplate identical across every input; the 19 remaining code_generation pairs come from a faulty regex extractor and are malformed. Do not train on this dataset.

defects.detail: Response is a fixed 3-line template ('It takes the parameters / It executes the logic / It returns the computed result') emitted identically for all 96 functions. Contains no information about the input function.
All 231 review pairs across 3 variants share a byte-identical response body. No bug, security or performance finding is derived from the submitted code.
Response is the ORIGINAL code returned unchanged, prefixed with comments asserting 'Added proper error handling' and 'Added input validation'. Trains the model to claim edits it did not make.

Generator regex in data/build_code_sft.py:9 mis-extracts. Observed instruction text is a fragment of the extractor's own pattern, e.g. 'Write a python function based on this description:\n(?:[^"]|"(?!""))*'. Extracted 'functions' also span multiple def statements.

secondary_findings.source_corpus: data/code_corpus_v0.jsonl (77 chunks, all source=local:* from this repository; 68 python / 9 javascript / 0 typescript)
secondary_findings.generation_claim_in_docs: docs/CODE_LLM_STRATEGY.md:74-84 claims 60,000 pairs distilled from DeepSeek-Coder/CodeLlama. No teacher model was used and no such volume exists.

remediation_required: Rewrite extraction with Python's ast module instead of regex.
Delete the three boilerplate generators, or replace them with a teacher model / external supervision.
Stop emitting refactor targets that assert changes not present in the response.
Regenerate at >=50k pairs from a real code corpus before any SFT run.
enforcement: training/sft.py refuses to train on a dataset with a sibling *.quarantine.json unless --ignore-sft-quarantine is passed.
